request.description:
Add a broker or paper account (saved to the config file, usable at once)

- An API key with the `admin` scope.
- This computer only: the Bridge refuses this call from any other address (403 `LOOPBACK_ONLY`).

Adds the account to the config file the Bridge loaded (or creates the per-user bridge.config.json when it started
without one), keeping the file's other content, and starts using it without a restart. New accounts are always
paper only: live trading is turned on only by editing the config file. Without `id` the Bridge picks
`<broker>-main`, then `<broker>-2` ... (`paper`, `paper-2` ... for paper accounts). Log in afterwards with
POST /v1/accounts/{accountId}/session. Admin scope with an admin key that may use every account, this computer
only. Audited as `account.added`.

Demo mode saves a real broker's account for the next normal start instead (`savedForLater: true`,
`account: null`): the same paper-only entry is written to the file, nothing is loaded and no broker is
contacted. `leaveDemo: true` also removes `"demo": true` from the file. Paper accounts are refused in demo mode
(it has its own), and so is everything when the demo dashboard is served to other computers.

request.description:
Place only the order that gets a position to a target size

- An API key with the `paper` scope (or `live`).
- Send an `Idempotency-Key` (8 to 255 characters); a retry with the same key returns the first result.

"Be long 3 lots", "be flat", "be short 50 shares", the way a strategy alert says it. The Bridge reads the current
position (this symbol, this product), works out the difference and places only that, through the same order
service as `POST /v1/orders`: the same safety gates, price checks, mode rules, confirmation rules and
idempotency. Paper unless you send `"mode": "live"`.

A position that cannot be read, or cannot be matched with certainty, is `POSITION_UNKNOWN` (503, safe to retry)
and nothing is placed: unknown is never treated as flat. Live delivery (CNC, MTF) that shows in both today's
positions and the holdings is also `POSITION_UNKNOWN`. An open order of the Bridge in the same symbol and product that
can change the position is `STATE_CONFLICT` unless you send `"openOrders": "ignore"` (a resting stop does not
count). `action` `NONE` places nothing and answers 200. With `dryRun` everything is worked out and checked
(the `preview` is the same result as `POST /v1/orders/preview`) and nothing is placed.

The `Idempotency-Key` (or `clientOrderId`) covers the whole request: a retry with the same body gets the first
answer back, including "nothing to do". Two requests for one symbol and product are handled one at a time.

request.description:
Place up to 20 independent orders in one call

- An API key with the `paper` scope (or `live`).
- Send an `Idempotency-Key` (8 to 255 characters); a retry with the same key returns the first result.

A convenience for alerts that need two legs (a hedge and a main order), not a strategy engine: the legs do not
know about each other and nothing is rolled back. Every leg goes through the same order service as
`POST /v1/orders` (same checks, safety gates, mode and confirmation rules), one after another, and each gets its
own entry in `results`, always in the order sent.

Nothing is hidden. The HTTP status is 201 only when every leg was placed; 207 when at least one leg went out (or
may have, `outcome_unknown`) and at least one did not; 422 when no leg went out. `data.ok`, `data.summary` and
each leg's `status` say the same. Leg `i` uses the request's `Idempotency-Key` plus `:i` as its own key, so a
retry cannot place a leg twice; a retry of the whole request with the same body gets the first answer back. A
batch where nothing went out may be retried with the same key. A live leg needs the key (or its own
`clientOrderId`). With `stopOnError`, legs after the first that did not go out are `skipped`.

item.name: Inbound alert (TradingView, signed generic, ChartInk or GoCharting)

request.description:
Inbound alert (TradingView, signed generic, ChartInk or GoCharting)

- No Bridge key. The hook token in the URL is the credential (generic hooks also need a signature).
- Served on the public ingress listener when it is enabled.

Answers within milliseconds (alert services give up after a few seconds) and processes the signal in the background,
through the same preview and safety checks as any order. The hook decides what an alert may do (account,
symbols, quantity caps, paper or live, whether a human must confirm). `generic` hooks must send
`X-MCB-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>">`; requests older than 5 minutes or
replayed are refused. Served on the public ingress listener when it is enabled.

`tradingview` hooks cannot sign (TradingView cannot add headers): the credential is the secret URL plus a
`passphrase` field inside the alert message (a JSON field, or `passphrase=...` in a plain-text alert), checked in
constant time before anything else is read. Wrong or missing: 401. The message is JSON (when TradingView sends
`application/json`) or one line of text (`text/plain`); see the `TradingViewAlert` schema. An alert older than
the hook's `maxAgeSec` (from its `time`) is refused with 400; a repeat of the same id + time + symbol + side is
acknowledged as `duplicate: true`. A rejected order after the 202 is shown in
`GET /v1/hooks/{hookId}/signals` and announced on the event bus as `hook.rejected`.
